description: Experience the rich, smoky flavors of authentic Tandoori Chicken, perfected on a charcoal grill. This classic Indian dish features succulent chicken marinated in a vibrant blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, then cooked to tender perfection with a beautiful charred finish. It is an irresistible centerpiece for any dinner, promising a taste of India in every bite.

ingredients.notes: skinned, bone-in, cut into 8-10 pieces or 4 leg quarters, deeply scored
thick, full-fat, preferably drained of excess water
Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat
freshly roasted and ground if possible

instructions.title: Prepare and First Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the chicken pieces and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make deep scores all over the chicken pieces. In a large bowl, combine the chicken with 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1 tsp salt. Rub well into the scores. Let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate large bowl, whisk together the plain yogurt, remaining 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, remaining 1 tbsp lemon juice, red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, remaining 0.5 tsp salt, and the optional red food color. Mix until a smooth, thick paste forms.

instructions.title: Second Marination
instructions.text: Add the pre-marinated chicken pieces to the yogurt-spice mixture. Add the mustard oil and rub the marinade generously into all the scores and over the entire surface of each chicken piece. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for the best flavor penetration.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: Arrange charcoal in your grill and light it, allowing it to heat until the coals are glowing red and covered with a fine layer of grey ash. This indicates medium-high heat. Ensure your grill grates are clean and lightly oiled to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly on the hot grill grate. Cook for about 20-25 minutes, turning occasionally to ensure even cooking and charring on all sides. Baste the chicken with any leftover marinade or a little oil during the last 10 minutes of cooking to keep it moist and enhance flavor.

instructions.title: Check for Doneness and Serve
instructions.text: The chicken is cooked when its internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) and the juices run clear. It should have a beautiful reddish-brown color with some charred spots. Remove from the grill, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges and cilantro.

tips: For truly authentic Tandoori flavor, ensure your yogurt is thick; draining it for an hour or two removes excess water, allowing the marinade to cling better to the chicken.
Do not skip the deep scoring of the chicken; this allows the marinade to penetrate deeply into the meat, ensuring maximum flavor and tenderness.
Serve Tandoori Chicken hot off the grill with fresh lemon wedges, a side of mint chutney, sliced onions, and naan bread or rice for a complete Indian meal experience.
article:
Unleash the tantalizing aromas and robust flavors of India right in your backyard with the ultimate guide to making Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This iconic dish, a jewel among Indian dinner recipes, is celebrated worldwide for its vibrant color, tender meat, and irresistible smoky char. While traditionally cooked in a clay tandoor oven, replicating that magic over a charcoal grill brings an unparalleled depth of flavor and a satisfying outdoor cooking experience that is simply unforgettable.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori chicken is a classic South Asian dish originating from the Indian subcontinent. It involves chicken marinated in yogurt and a blend of spices, then traditionally cooked at high temperatures in a tandoor, a cylindrical clay oven. The intense heat of the tandoor cooks the chicken quickly, sealing in juices while imparting a distinctive smoky flavor and a beautiful charred exterior. When we talk about Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, we're aiming to recreate this authentic experience using a standard charcoal grill. The charcoal embers provide a dry, intense heat source and, crucially, infuse the chicken with that beloved smoky essence that sets it apart from oven-baked or gas-grilled versions. It’s a healthy, protein-rich dish that makes a spectacular centerpiece for any Indian dinner, embodying the heart and soul of traditional Indian cuisine.

## Ingredients You Need for Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken

Crafting the perfect Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken starts with a stellar marinade. Here's what you'll need:

*   **Chicken:** 2-3 lbs chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or a mix, skin removed). Bone-in pieces are traditional and retain moisture better.
*   **Yogurt:** 1 cup full-fat plain yogurt (Greek yogurt works well for a thicker marinade).
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 2 tablespoons (freshly made is best).
*   **Lemon Juice:** 2 tablespoons, freshly squeezed.
*   **Spice Blend (Tandoori Masala):**
    *   2 teaspoons ground cumin
    *   2 teaspoons ground coriander
    *   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
    *   1 teaspoon garam masala
    *   1 teaspoon red chili powder (adjust to your spice preference)
    *   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
    *   1/2 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
    *   1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika (for extra color and smoky notes)
*   **Salt:** 1-2 teaspoons, or to taste.
*   **Food Coloring (Optional):** A few drops of red or orange food coloring for the classic vibrant hue. Turmeric and paprika provide natural color, but artificial coloring enhances it.
*   **Oil:** 2 tablespoons vegetable or mustard oil (for basting).

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Grilling Tandoori Chicken

Making Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a process that rewards patience and attention to detail.

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep slits on each piece of chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor and even cooking.
2.  **Make the Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, all the dry spices (cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, chili powder, black pepper, fenugreek, smoked paprika), and salt. If using, add the food coloring now. Mix everything thoroughly until you have a smooth, well-combined paste.
3.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the prepared chicken pieces to the marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated. Use your hands to really work the marinade into the slits. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 6-8 hours, or ideally overnight (up to 24 hours). The longer the marination, the more tender and flavorful your chicken will be.
4.  **Prepare the Grill:** Arrange charcoal in your grill. For indirect grilling, push the coals to one side. For direct grilling, spread them evenly. Light the charcoal and let it burn until covered with a thin layer of grey ash, indicating medium-high heat. Clean your grill grates and oil them well to prevent sticking.
5.  **Grill the Chicken:**
    *   Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the medium-high heat. If using bone-in pieces, you might start them over direct heat to get a good char, then move them to indirect heat to cook through without burning.
    *   Grill for 5-7 minutes per side over direct heat, turning frequently to prevent burning and achieve an even char.
    *   Once a good char has developed, move the chicken to the cooler, indirect heat zone (if applicable) or reduce the heat by adjusting vents.
    *   Continue grilling, turning and basting occasionally with oil, until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) when checked with a meat thermometer. This usually takes 20-30 minutes in total, depending on the size of the chicken pieces and grill temperature. The chicken should be cooked through, juicy on the inside, with a beautiful smoky, slightly charred exterior.
6.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and moist chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken

*   **Dry Chicken is Key:** Before marinating, ensure your chicken is thoroughly dry. Excess moisture will dilute the marinade and prevent a good sear.
*   **Deep Slits:** Don't be shy with the slits! They are crucial for the marinade to penetrate deeply into the meat, ensuring flavor in every bite of your Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken.
*   **Full-Fat Yogurt:** Use full-fat yogurt as it helps tenderize the chicken without breaking down too much. Greek yogurt is excellent for a thick, clingy marinade.
*   **Marination Time:** Don't skimp on marination. Overnight is ideal for maximum flavor infusion and tenderness.
*   **Temperature Control:** Charcoal grilling requires attention. Start with medium-high heat for charring, then manage the heat to cook the chicken through without burning. Use a grill with adjustable vents to control airflow and temperature.
*   **Don't Overcrowd:** Grill in batches if necessary. Overcrowding the grill lowers the temperature and steams the chicken instead of grilling it, preventing that desired smoky char.
*   **Basting:** Basting with a little oil during the later stages of grilling helps keep the chicken moist and promotes a beautiful golden-brown finish.
*   **Resting:** Always rest your cooked chicken. This step is vital for juicy, tender results.

## Serving Suggestions for Tandoori Chicken

Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of Indian accompaniments, creating a complete and satisfying Indian dinner.

*   **Breads:** Serve hot with freshly baked naan, roti, or paratha to soak up all the flavorful juices.
*   **Rice:** A side of basmati rice, jeera rice (cumin rice), or a light vegetable pulao complements the chicken perfectly.
*   **Chutneys and Dips:** Mint chutney, cilantro chutney, or a cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) are essential for dipping.
*   **Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice and spices) adds a refreshing crunch.
*   **Lemon and Onion:** Always serve with fresh lemon wedges for squeezing over the chicken and some thinly sliced red onion rings for a sharp contrast.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a masterpiece, you can explore several variations:

*   **Boneless Chicken:** Use boneless chicken thighs or breasts for quicker cooking. Just be careful not to overcook them to maintain juiciness.
*   **Whole Chicken:** For a show-stopping meal, spatchcock a whole chicken and marinate it. Adjust grilling time accordingly.
*   **Vegetarian Tandoori:** The same marinade can be used for paneer (Indian cheese), mushrooms, bell peppers, onions, or cauliflower florets to create delicious vegetarian tandoori skewers.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the red chili powder to suit your palate. For more heat, add green chilies to the ginger-garlic paste. For less, reduce the chili powder or omit it.
*   **Alternative Grilling Methods:** While charcoal grilling offers the best flavor, you can use a gas grill (ensure good ventilation for smoke flavor), an oven (broil for char), or even an air fryer for a quicker, less smoky version. However, for that truly authentic smoky taste, nothing beats the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken experience.

Embracing the art of making Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken at home is a rewarding culinary journey. The smoky aroma, the tender meat, and the burst of authentic Indian spices create a dish that truly stands out. It's more than just a meal; it's an experience that brings the vibrant flavors of India to your dinner table, promising a delightful feast for family and friends. So fire up your grill and prepare to be amazed by the deliciousness of homemade Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken.
